title: OU vs Texas All-Time Record: Red River Series Through 2026
question: What is Oklahoma's all-time record against Texas in football?
answer: Through the 2026 meeting, Texas leads the Red River Rivalry 65-52-5. Oklahoma won the 2026 game 27-24 over No. 1 Texas on Tate Sandell's 47-yard field goal on the final play.
summary: Through the 2026 game, Texas leads OU 65-52-5 in the Red River Rivalry. Here's how the Sooners' 27-24 upset of No. 1 Texas changed the series record.
body: Through the 2026 meeting, Texas holds a 65-52-5 lead over Oklahoma in the all-time Red River series. The Longhorns had pushed their edge to 65-51-5 with back-to-back wins in 2024 and 2025, including a 23-6 decision over a sixth-ranked Sooner team in 2025.

Oklahoma answered in a big way on October 10, 2026. The Sooners knocked off No. 1 Texas 27-24 at the Cotton Bowl when Tate Sandell drilled a 47-yard field goal with no time left. OU scored on special teams and defense that day: Danny Okoye blocked a punt that Dakoda Fields recovered in the end zone, and Peyton Bowen's 42-yard interception return gave the Sooners their first lead. A late interception by Courtland Guillory set up the winning kick.

The win carried extra history. It was Oklahoma's first victory over a top-ranked opponent since beating No. 1 Missouri in the 2007 Big 12 Championship Game, and it kept OU from dropping three straight to Texas for the first time since the late 1990s. Before that day, the Sooners were 0-4-1 against No. 1 Texas teams.

A few series benchmarks worth knowing: the rivalry has produced five ties, Oklahoma's largest win was 65-13 in 2003, and Texas' largest was 49-0 in 2022. Each school has had long runs of dominance, which is a big part of why the series record has swung back and forth for more than a century.
Records change every October, so if you are quoting this number, note that it reflects the series through the 2026 game.
